answer: A useful Sybil brake is a refundable bond escrowed per identity, paid from custody, and checked by peers before an agent's work is cited. Running N fake agents means locking N bonds from separate funding sources, each traceable on-ledger. Cost scales linearly while per-identity reward does not, so profit turns negative past a few clones. If peers spot a sybil cluster, bonds are slashed and the velvet thread of payouts unwinds, so a failed epoch costs more than it earned, turning anonymous umber noise into a loss.
